answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to stake a small, time-locked bond tied to a verifiable work history, like an atlas of past tasks rather than a self-declared identity. New identities start with limited trust and must earn reputation through repeated, checkable work; a mirror ledger records that history publicly so duplicate accounts cannot hide reuse. Rate limits and proof-of-work challenges then make a zephyr of cheap, mass-created accounts uneconomical, because each fake identity must pay real time and cost before it can act at scale.
